aPropos.title: About us
aPropos.intro: Karriere Fähre is an international placement agency based in Douala, Cameroon, founded by a German-French-Cameroonian entrepreneur.
aPropos.missionBody: Building a reliable bridge between talent from Central Africa and German companies facing a skilled-labor shortage, through training, integration preparation, and support at every step of placement.
aPropos.founderTitle: A founder who knows both sides
aPropos.founderBody: Having grown up between Germany and Cameroon, our founder understands both the demands of the German labor market and the aspirations of Cameroonian talent. Karriere Fähre (literally "the career ferry") carries that bridge in its name.
aPropos.value2: High standards in training and candidate preparation
aPropos.distingueLead: An agency built for both shores, with a genuine command of the German framework.
aPropos.dist1Body: Rooted in Central Africa and connected to the real needs of German companies.
aPropos.dist2Body: Skilled Immigration Act, Chancenkarte, qualification recognition (Anerkennung).
aPropos.dist3Body: From A1 up to the required level, supporting even candidates starting from scratch.
aPropos.dist4Body: Recruitment that respects people and origin countries alike, for the long term.
aPropos.ethiqueTitle: Ethical recruitment, on both sides of the bridge
aPropos.ethiqueHeading: We follow the WHO Code of Practice
aPropos.ethiqueBody1: International recruitment of professionals, especially in healthcare, must be responsible. We rely on the WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel: we don't recruit at the expense of countries whose essential systems are fragile.
aPropos.ethiqueBody2: In practice, that means transparent pathways, informed candidate consent, and a win-win relationship between Central Africa and Germany.
aPropos.ethiqueNote: Reference: WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel.
aPropos.equipeLead: A German-Cameroonian team that knows both realities: that of African talent and that of German employers.
aPropos.equipeNote: This section will be completed with real photos and team bios before launch.
aPropos.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about Karriere Fähre
aPropos.doorsTitle: Which side of the bridge are you on?
aPropos.doorsText: Whether you want to work or train in Germany, or you're looking to recruit, we support you.
aPropos.doorsCandidat: I want to work / train in Germany

aProposFaq.a1: Karriere Fähre is a German-Cameroonian placement agency based in Douala. We connect qualified talent and aspiring trainees from Central Africa with German companies facing labor shortages, with German training and full support.
aProposFaq.q2: What does the name "Karriere Fähre" mean?
aProposFaq.a2: "Karriere" means "career" and "Fähre" means "ferry" in German. Together: "the career ferry", the image of a boat connecting two shores, just as we connect Central Africa and Germany.
aProposFaq.a3: Our agency is based in Douala, Cameroon, with a primary focus on Central Africa and a direct connection to the needs of German companies.
aProposFaq.a4: Yes. We rely on the WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel, so as not to weaken essential systems in origin countries and to ensure transparent, consented pathways.
aProposFaq.q5: Do you support candidates who don't speak German yet?
aProposFaq.a5: Yes. We offer built-in language training, from A1 up to the level required by the trade, supporting even candidates starting from scratch.

aProposHistoire.title: Our story
aProposHistoire.subtitle: How Karriere Fähre grew out of a journey between two countries.
aProposHistoire.section1Body: Our founder grew up between Germany and Cameroon. She saw, on one side, German companies struggling to hire for essential jobs, and on the other, Cameroonian talent ready to train and contribute, but without a reliable bridge to connect them.
aProposHistoire.section2Body: Karriere Fähre was founded in Douala to close that gap: an organization that knows German requirements (language, qualification recognition, legal framework) and Cameroonian realities (training, support, trust) from the inside.
aProposHistoire.section3Body: "Fähre" means "ferry" in German. Like a ferry connects two shores, Karriere Fähre connects two labor markets, one candidate and one company at a time.

aProposMethode.title: Our method
aProposMethode.subtitle: A structured process, from first contact through to integration in Germany.
aProposMethode.section1Body: Every candidate takes a German placement test before any placement promise is made. We guide them to the right path, Fast Track or Full Training, rather than making unrealistic claims.
aProposMethode.section2Body: Our German courses follow the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR), with preparation for exams recognized by employers and German authorities.
aProposMethode.section3Body: On the company side, every account is validated by our team before any access to the candidate pool. On the candidate side, every profile is reviewed before becoming visible to partner companies.
aProposMethode.section4Body: Our role doesn't stop at the signed contract: we stay available during visa procedures and the first steps in Germany.

candidats.title: Working or training in Germany, supported at every step
candidats.subtitle: In short: there are three legal paths to working in Germany from Cameroon: skilled employment, vocational training (Ausbildung), and the Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte). Karriere Fähre assesses your profile, trains you in German, and prepares every step up to departure.
candidats.kick: Candidate area · Cameroon & Central Africa → Germany
candidats.voiesTitle: What are the paths to working in Germany?
candidats.voiesLead: Three legal paths lead to Germany, depending on your qualification, experience, and German level. Here's how they differ, and which one fits you.
candidats.voie1Body: You already have a recognized qualification or professional experience.
candidats.voie2Body: You're young and want to learn a trade on the job, directly within a company.
candidats.voie3Body: You want to come look for a job on the ground, with no contract at departure.
candidats.voie3Tag2: Up to 1 year on-site to search
candidats.tableRow2Val2: B2 with us · legal minimum B1
candidats.tableRow5Val3: Up to 12 months to find work
candidats.tableNote: The exact thresholds (points, language level per occupation) evolve with German regulations. We check them for your case during the assessment.
candidats.eligibiliteTitle: Am I eligible to work in Germany?
candidats.eligibiliteLead: You're likely eligible if you're between 18 and about 40, have a qualification or professional experience, and are willing to learn German up to the required level. Four things matter:
candidats.crit1Body: A qualification (even a Cameroonian one) or solid experience in a sought-after trade. We help get it recognized.
candidats.crit2Body: B2 is our own standard, for skilled employment and for the Ausbildung alike. The legal minimum for the Ausbildung visa is usually B1, but we prepare you to B2: that's what makes the difference on arrival. Don't have it yet? Our courses take you there from scratch.
candidats.crit3Body: Most paths target 18-40 year-olds, with Ausbildung geared more toward younger candidates. Each case is reviewed individually.
candidats.crit4Body: Success depends as much on preparation as on drive. We support those who commit seriously.
candidats.quizTitle: Full Training or Fast Track: which path is right for you?
candidats.quizSubtitle: Answer in 30 seconds to discover the training path suited to your level.
candidats.quizQ1Title: What is your current German level?
candidats.quizQ2Title: Do you hold a German certification (Goethe / telc)?
candidats.quizQ2Opt1: Yes, a B2 less than 12 months old
candidats.quizQ2Opt2: Yes, a B2 more than 12 months old
candidats.quizQ3Opt2: I'm already fluent, I want to work fast
candidats.quizResultFastTrackTitle: You're ready for the Fast Track
candidats.quizResultFastTrackText: You hold a currently valid B2 certificate. We prepare you directly for employment: integration course, professional German, and interview coaching (4 individual sessions).
candidats.quizResultExamPrepText: You have the level, but need a currently valid B2 certificate (a B2 certificate expires after 12 months). A short Goethe/telc exam prep track lets you obtain or renew it before moving on to the Fast Track.
candidats.quizResultB1ToB2Text: You're missing one step. A targeted Full Training path (B1 → B2, with exam prep) brings you to the required level before moving on to job preparation.
candidats.quizResultFullTrainingTitle: The Full Training path is made for you
candidats.quizResultFullTrainingText: You're starting from scratch or close to it. Our complete path trains you from A1 to B2 (11 months, 880 hours), with Goethe/telc exam preparation, followed by job preparation.
candidats.quizNote: Indicative result. An official placement test will confirm your path during your profile assessment.
candidats.legalQuizTitle: Which legal path fits your profile?
candidats.legalQuizSubtitle: Based on official German criteria (residence law, Auswärtiges Amt) for skilled employment, the Chancenkarte, and Ausbildung.
candidats.legalQuizQ1Title: Do you already have a concrete job offer from a German company?
candidats.legalQuizQ1Opt1: Yes, I have a job offer
candidats.legalQuizQ2Opt3: Vocational training of 2 years or more
candidats.legalQuizQ3Title: What is your current German level?
candidats.legalQuizResultEmploiTitle: You meet the criteria for skilled employment
candidats.legalQuizResultEmploiText: With a job offer and a recognizable university degree or vocational qualification, you can aim directly for the skilled-worker residence permit: the fastest path, with no age limit.
candidats.legalQuizResultEmploiRef: Legal basis: §§ 18a and 18b of the German Residence Act (AufenthG), criteria from the Federal Foreign Office (Auswärtiges Amt).
candidats.legalQuizResultChancenkarteText: You have a recognizable qualification but no job offer yet: the Chancenkarte (Opportunity Card) lets you come look for a job on-site. Admission is based on a points system (qualification, German/English, experience, age); a minimum of 6 points is required.
candidats.legalQuizResultChancenkarteRef: Legal basis: §§ 20a and 20b AufenthG, detailed points system on the official Make it in Germany portal.
candidats.legalQuizResultAusbildungTitle: Ausbildung is the best-suited path for your profile
candidats.legalQuizResultAusbildungText: With no prior qualification and under 35, vocational apprenticeship training (Ausbildung) is your entry path: it requires no starting diploma. The legal minimum for the entry visa is usually B1 — at Karriere Fähre we prepare you to B2, so you understand your colleagues and your trainer from day one.
candidats.legalQuizResultAusbildungRef: Legal basis: § 16a AufenthG. Age limit raised to 35 since the March 2024 reform.
candidats.legalQuizResultConseillerBadge: A conversation with an advisor is needed
candidats.legalQuizResultConseillerTitle: Your situation calls for a personalized review
candidats.legalQuizResultConseillerText: Without a recognizable qualification and past the Ausbildung age limit, or with a profile close to the Chancenkarte points threshold, no path can be recommended automatically. One of our advisors can review your situation in detail and identify realistic options.
candidats.legalQuizResultConseillerRef: Every case is unique: partial diploma recognition, uncertified experience, or a shortage occupation can change the outcome.
candidats.legalQuizAdvisorCta: Book an appointment with an advisor
candidats.legalQuizNote: Indicative result based on general legal criteria. Your full file (diploma, experience, sector) is reviewed precisely during your profile assessment.

candidatsComment.title: How it works
candidatsComment.subtitle: Four clear steps between your sign-up and your departure for Germany.
candidatsComment.section1Body: You create your candidate profile and take a German placement test, oral and written.
candidatsComment.section2Body: Already B2: you join our candidate pool directly. Below B2: you follow our full A1 → B2 training program.
candidatsComment.section3Body: Once your profile is validated by our team, it becomes visible to our German partner companies looking for your skills.
candidatsComment.section4Body: Visa procedures, departure preparation, first steps in Germany: we stay by your side at every stage.

candidatsEligibilite.title: Am I eligible?
candidatsEligibilite.subtitle: The basic criteria for joining the Karriere Fähre program.
candidatsEligibilite.section1Body: Be of legal age and have a serious plan to train or settle professionally in Germany.
candidatsEligibilite.section2Body: No level is required at sign-up. If you're already at B2, you go straight to placement. Otherwise, you follow our A1 → B2 training path.
candidatsEligibilite.section3Body: We prioritize shortage occupations in Germany: healthcare, hospitality, construction, industry and technical trades, IT. A qualification or experience in one of these fields is an advantage.
candidatsEligibilite.section4Title: Not sure? Let's talk it through
candidatsEligibilite.section4Body: The best way to know where you stand is a direct conversation. Book an appointment, no obligation.

candidatsDiplomes.title: Qualification recognition
candidatsDiplomes.subtitle: What to know before getting your qualification recognized in Germany.
candidatsDiplomes.section1Body: For many regulated occupations (healthcare in particular), Germany requires your diploma to be recognized as equivalent to a German one before you can practice.
candidatsDiplomes.section2Body: We help you identify the right authority for your occupation and target region, gather the right documents, and anticipate any upskilling measures required.
candidatsDiplomes.section3Title: What this means for your timeline
candidatsDiplomes.section3Body: Recognition can take several months. We factor it into your path from the start to avoid surprises on the visa and employer side.

candidatsVivre.title: Living in Germany
candidatsVivre.subtitle: What to expect once you're there, beyond the job.
candidatsVivre.section1Body: Registering with local authorities (Anmeldung), opening a bank account, finding housing: we prepare you for these steps before departure.
candidatsVivre.section2Body: B2 level lets you work, but daily life keeps demanding effort. We encourage continued learning once you're there.
candidatsVivre.section3Body: Karriere Fähre stays reachable after your arrival to guide you through any question or integration difficulty.

candidatsFaq.title: Candidate FAQ
candidatsFaq.subtitle: The most frequently asked questions about our program.
candidatsFaq.q1: Is Karriere Fähre paid for candidates?
candidatsFaq.a1: Terms vary by path (Fast Track or Full Training). Contact us or book an appointment to discuss the details.
candidatsFaq.q2: Do I need to already speak German to sign up?
candidatsFaq.a2: No. You can sign up with no prior knowledge and follow our full A1 → B2 path.
candidatsFaq.q3: How long does the full path take?
candidatsFaq.a3: About 10 months of training (A1 to B2), plus 1 month of exam preparation.
candidatsFaq.q4: Does Karriere Fähre guarantee a job in Germany?
candidatsFaq.a4: We guarantee serious support and matching with real partner companies. Final placement also depends on your profile and the interview with the employer.
candidatsFaq.a5: We prioritize shortage occupations in Germany (healthcare, hospitality, construction, industry, IT). Your profile and preferences are taken into account during matching.
candidatsFaq.q6: What happens if I don't reach B2 level?
candidatsFaq.a6: We adjust the training pace. Placement only happens once the required level is reached.

coursAllemand.title: German course: from A1 to B2, up to the level Germany requires
coursAllemand.subtitle: In short: an intensive course structured around the Common European Framework (CEFR), roughly 10 months from beginner to B2, plus one month of exam preparation. Even starting from zero.
coursAllemand.pourquoiTitle: Your German level decides which route is open to you
coursAllemand.pourquoiLead: German isn't a formality: it's the criterion that opens or closes each route to Germany. Here's what each one requires.
coursAllemand.voie1Body: B2 required, along with a recognised qualification or relevant experience.
coursAllemand.voie2Body: B2 required with us to start a dual apprenticeship; the legal visa minimum is usually B1.
coursAllemand.voie3Body: A1 minimum: the higher your level, the more points you score.
coursAllemand.voiesNote: Exact thresholds shift with German regulations and the target occupation. We check them for your case during the assessment.
coursAllemand.parcoursLead: Each stage follows the CEFR, runs as a group, and has a fixed number of hours. You move up one level at a time until B2.
coursAllemand.a1Body: Understand and use familiar everyday expressions, introduce yourself, ask simple questions about your immediate surroundings.
coursAllemand.a2Body: Understand isolated sentences on close-to-home topics (family, shopping, work), exchange simple information about routine tasks.
coursAllemand.b1Body: Cope on your own in most everyday situations, produce simple connected speech, describe an event and explain a plan.
coursAllemand.b2Body: Understand the main ideas of concrete and abstract topics, interact with a native speaker fluently and spontaneously. This is the level expected to work.
coursAllemand.prepBody: A dedicated month after B2, focused on the format of your chosen exam: comprehension, written and spoken production, time management.
coursAllemand.totalNote: That's roughly 10 months of teaching, plus 1 month of exam preparation.
coursAllemand.metierTitle: German aimed at your occupation, not just at grammar
coursAllemand.metierBody1: Beyond general language, our courses cover the professional vocabulary of your sector and real everyday situations in Germany.
coursAllemand.metierBody2: Student file, badge, tracked attendance: we prepare our candidates with the same rigour expected in a German workplace.
coursAllemand.examensTitle: A certificate recognised by employers and authorities
coursAllemand.examensLead: Goethe-Institut, TELC, ÖSD, TestDaF for B2. A B1 exam is available on request. We point you to whichever fits your target occupation and region.
coursAllemand.inc1: Opening and managing your student file
coursAllemand.inc3: Student kit: badge, house rules, teaching materials, student guide
coursAllemand.inc4: Access to the online student area
coursAllemand.pricingNote: For fees and payment terms, contact us or book an appointment.
coursAllemand.fastTrackTitle: Already B2? You don't need this course
coursAllemand.fastTrackBody: If you already have B2 (certified or not), you can join our candidate pool directly for placement with our partner companies in Germany.
coursAllemand.finalText: We assess your real level, spoken and written, then place you in the right group — starting at A1 if you're beginning from zero.

ausbildung.title: Ausbildung in Germany: learn a trade, paid, with no qualification to start
ausbildung.subtitle: In short: the Ausbildung is Germany's dual vocational training. Three years split between a company and a vocational school, a salary from the first month, a recognised qualification at the end — and no qualification needed to begin.
ausbildung.ctaEval: Check whether the Ausbildung is my route
ausbildung.quoiTitle: An Ausbildung is not an internship
ausbildung.quoiLead: It's the German vocational training system, and the most common way in for a young person who hasn't trained in a trade yet.
ausbildung.quoi1Title: You're an employee, not a student
ausbildung.quoi1Body: You sign a training contract with a German company and are paid every month, from the first year.
ausbildung.quoi2Body: You learn the trade on the job at the company, and the theory at the vocational school (Berufsschule).
ausbildung.quoi3Title: A recognised qualification at the end
ausbildung.quoi3Body: After three years you hold a qualification recognised across Germany — and you become a Fachkraft.
ausbildung.conditionsTitle: What you need to line up for an Ausbildung
ausbildung.conditionsLead: Less demanding on qualifications than people assume, more demanding on language and age.
ausbildung.cond1Body: That's the whole point of this route: you don't need a recognised qualification to start. A secondary school leaving certificate is enough.
ausbildung.cond2Body: The age limit for the Ausbildung visa was raised to 35 in March 2024 (§ 16a of the German Residence Act).
ausbildung.cond3Body: The legal minimum for the visa is usually B1. At Karriere Fähre we prepare you to B2: that's what lets you follow the vocational school and understand your trainer from day one.
ausbildung.cond4Body: You need a contract with a German company before you leave. That is exactly what we go and find for you.
ausbildung.conditionsNote: Exact thresholds shift with German regulations, the trade, and the chamber responsible. We check them for your case during the assessment.
ausbildung.langueBody1: Without the language there is no visa, no training place, and no vocational school you could follow. It's the first step, and it's the one we walk with you from zero.
ausbildung.langueBody2: Our course takes you from A1 to B2 in roughly 10 months, plus one month of exam preparation.
ausbildung.salaireLead: Unlike conventional studies, the Ausbildung pays you a monthly salary from the first year, with a minimum set by German law.
ausbildung.etapesTitle: From your application to your first day
ausbildung.etape1Body: Age, schooling, motivation: we check that the Ausbildung really is your route.
ausbildung.etape2Body: From A1 to B2, with the vocabulary of the trade you're aiming for.
ausbildung.etape3Body: We put your profile in front of German companies hiring apprentices.
ausbildung.etape4Body: Training contract signed, then the Ausbildung visa file and the embassy appointment.
ausbildung.etape5Body: Settling in, first days at the company and the school, and our follow-up on the ground.
ausbildung.apresTitle: The Ausbildung isn't an end, it's a way in
ausbildung.apresBody1: After three years your qualification is recognised in Germany: you become a Fachkraft, on a qualified professional's salary and a residence permit tied to your job.
ausbildung.apresBody2: That's the difference from leaving without a qualification: you don't start from zero, you build a career.
ausbildung.finalText: The legal routes test answers that in four questions, based on the official German criteria.
ausbildung.employeurNote: Are you a company whose Ausbildung places stay vacant?

ausbildungSalaire.title: Ausbildung pay: how much does an apprentice earn in Germany?
ausbildungSalaire.subtitle: In short: apprentices are paid monthly from the first year. German law sets a floor — €724 gross in year one for contracts starting in 2026 — and the real average sits well above it.
ausbildungSalaire.minTitle: The minimum set by German law
ausbildungSalaire.minLead: The Mindestausbildungsvergütung is the legal minimum, revised every year. These amounts apply to training starting between 1 January and 31 December 2026.
ausbildungSalaire.minNote: Source: Bundesinstitut für Berufsbildung (BIBB), based on the Vocational Training Act (BBiG). Gross amounts, for contracts starting in 2026.
ausbildungSalaire.moyLead: The legal minimum is a floor, not a norm. At companies covered by a collective agreement, the average is considerably higher.
ausbildungSalaire.moyBody: In 2025, average apprentice pay at companies under a collective agreement reached €1,209 gross per month, up 6.7% year on year. The gap between western (€1,208) and eastern Germany (€1,213) has all but disappeared.
ausbildungSalaire.moyNote: Source: BIBB survey of collectively agreed apprenticeship pay, data as of 1 October 2025. These figures cover companies bound by a collective agreement.
ausbildungSalaire.varie1Body: The spread between trades is wide: construction, industry and the public sector generally pay better than parts of the crafts sector.
ausbildungSalaire.varie2Body: Pay rises with each year, as the table above shows.
ausbildungSalaire.varie3Body: A company outside a collective agreement may pay less, but no more than 20% below the agreed rates for its sector and region.
ausbildungSalaire.varie4Body: These are gross amounts. Social contributions and tax are deducted afterwards, depending on your situation.
ausbildungSalaire.disclaimer: These amounts are public German data (BIBB, BBiG), provided for information. They are not salaries guaranteed by Karriere Fähre: your pay will be stated in the training contract you sign with your company.
ausbildungSalaire.finalTitle: See whether the Ausbildung is your route
ausbildungSalaire.finalText: Pay is only one criterion. The legal routes test checks your actual eligibility in four questions.

formationsAllemand.title: German courses A1 → B2
formationsAllemand.subtitle: The core of our Full Training path, from the very first course to the level required to work in Germany.
formationsAllemand.section1Body: A1, A2, B1, then B2: each level follows the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR), with groups progressing together over about 2 to 3 months per stage.
formationsAllemand.section2Title: Courses built for the German context
formationsAllemand.section2Body: Beyond grammar and vocabulary, our courses include professional vocabulary and everyday situations you'll face in Germany.
formationsAllemand.section3Body: Student file, badge, tracked attendance: we prepare our candidates with the same rigor expected in a German professional setting.

formationsExamens.title: Exam preparation
formationsExamens.subtitle: Goethe-Institut, TELC, ÖSD, TestDaF: exams recognized by employers and German authorities.
formationsExamens.section1Body: A recognized certificate (usually B2 level) is generally required for the work visa and directly reassures the employer about your actual level.
formationsExamens.section2Title: One dedicated month, at the end of the path
formationsExamens.section2Body: After reaching B2, one month of intensive preparation (about 80 hours) prepares you specifically for the format of your chosen exam.
formationsExamens.section3Body: We guide you toward the exam best suited to your target occupation and destination region. A B1-level exam is available on request.

formationsIntegration.title: Upskilling & integration
formationsIntegration.subtitle: Preparing to live and work in Germany, not just to speak the language.
formationsIntegration.section1Body: German workplace norms, punctuality, communicating with an employer, administrative life: we cover these topics during training, not just right before departure.
formationsIntegration.section2Body: If you already have some German but targeted gaps, we offer a shorter upskilling track instead of repeating the full A1 → B2 path.
formationsIntegration.section3Body: This preparation continues after your arrival in Germany, alongside our post-departure support.

entreprises.title: Recruit skilled talent from Central Africa, with confidence
entreprises.subtitle: In short: we select, train, and prepare qualified, motivated candidates, linguistically, professionally, and culturally, in line with the Skilled Immigration Act. You receive profiles ready to join your teams.
entreprises.kick: Employer area · Recruitment from Central Africa
entreprises.probTitle: Is the labor shortage slowing your business down?
entreprises.probBody1: Unfilled roles, strained schedules, slowed growth: the lack of skilled staff costs German companies dearly. Local recruitment alone is no longer enough.
entreprises.probBody2: Karriere Fähre opens a pool of motivated talent from Central Africa, prepared to integrate into your teams for the long term.
entreprises.probStat1Label: of unfilled skilled positions in Germany (official sources)
entreprises.probStat2Label: healthcare, construction, industry, hospitality, IT, logistics
entreprises.pourquoiLead: A single partner, from finding the right profile through to lasting integration.
entreprises.pil1Body: Trained in German (up to B2), prepared for their trade and for German workplace culture. No integration left to chance.
entreprises.pil2Body: Qualification recognition, skilled worker visa, accelerated procedure: we secure every step.
entreprises.pil3Body: As a German-Cameroonian agency, we understand both sides: the reality of candidates and the expectations of German employers.
entreprises.secteursTitle: A response tailored to your business
entreprises.secteursLead: Every sector has its own constraints. We adapt profiles and preparation to your reality.
entreprises.seg1Body: Hospitals, clinics, and care homes: schedule coverage, staffing ratios, continuity of care.
entreprises.seg2Body: Hotels and restaurants: seasonality, strained service, roles in direct contact with customers.
entreprises.seg3Body: Construction and technical trades: scarce skilled labor, strained job sites.
entreprises.seg4Body: Factories, tech, and transport: a need for technicians, digital profiles, and drivers.
entreprises.servicesLead: From finding the right profile through to integration, we handle the whole chain: you keep one single point of contact.
entreprises.srv1Body: Identification and assessment of qualified, motivated candidates based on your needs.
entreprises.srv2Body: German up to the required level, Goethe/telc exam preparation, trade-specific upskilling.
entreprises.srv3Body: Qualification recognition, visa file and procedure, fully compliant.
entreprises.srv4Body: Support after arrival, for a successful, lasting integration.
entreprises.profilsLead: Qualified profiles in the sectors under the most pressure in Germany.
entreprises.besoinsTitle: Hire a qualified professional or train an apprentice
entreprises.besoinsLead: Whether you need someone operational from day one or want to train the next generation, we draw on two distinct talent pools.
entreprises.besoin1Body: Care assistants, technicians, cooks, drivers: candidates who already hold a qualification or relevant experience, trained in German to the level your role requires. We handle qualification recognition and the skilled worker visa.
entreprises.besoin1Tag2: German to the required level (often B2)
entreprises.besoin1Tag3: Recognition and visa handled by us
entreprises.besoin2Body: Are your Ausbildung places still vacant at the start of the intake? We introduce young, motivated candidates prepared for the language and for German working culture, ready for a dual apprenticeship at your company.
entreprises.besoin2Tag2: German at the required level before arrival
entreprises.pourquoiAfriqueBody1: Central Africa has a large, qualified, and highly motivated young population looking to build a lasting career. French-speaking and trained in German by us, these candidates integrate with seriousness and a genuine life plan, not just a passing opportunity.
entreprises.pourquoiAfriqueBody2: Our source countries: Cameroon (base), Gabon, Congo, Chad, Equatorial Guinea, Central African Republic, and, in English, beyond Central Africa.
entreprises.modelesTitle: The model that fits your urgency
entreprises.modelesLead: Depending on your need, we offer either already-ready profiles or tailored training.
entreprises.modele1Body: Candidates who already have the required German level and a recognized qualification.
entreprises.modele1Tag1: Selection from our pool of ready profiles
entreprises.modele2Body: We train promising candidates up to exactly the level your roles require.
entreprises.modele2Tag1: German upskilling (up to B2) + trade preparation
entreprises.processusLead: A clear, secure process, from analyzing your need through to lasting integration, in line with the German legal framework.
entreprises.proc1Body: Roles, expected skills, timeline, and required language level.
entreprises.proc2Body: Identification and assessment of qualified, motivated profiles in our pool.
entreprises.proc3Body: You meet the shortlisted candidates and confirm your choices.
entreprises.proc4Body: German up to the required level, Goethe/telc exams, and trade upskilling.
entreprises.proc5Body: Recognition procedure, possible on-site via the Anerkennungspartnerschaft.
entreprises.proc6Body: Skilled worker visa file and procedure, accelerable via § 81a.
entreprises.proc7Body: Settling in, onboarding, and follow-up for integration that lasts.
entreprises.cadreTitle: The German legal framework, mastered end to end
entreprises.cadreLead: The Skilled Immigration Act, reformed in 2023-2024, opens three paths. We know each one and choose the fastest and safest for your recruitment.
entreprises.cadre1Body: Fachkräfte (recognized qualification), Berufserfahrung (qualifying experience), and Potenzial (Chancenkarte, points-based). We guide each candidate to the best-suited path.
entreprises.cadre2Body: As an employer, you can launch the accelerated skilled worker procedure with the central authority: recognition and visa are processed as a priority.
entreprises.cadre3Body: New in 2024: the Anerkennungspartnerschaft allows the candidate to come first, then finalize qualification recognition on-site.
entreprises.cadreNote: What this means for you: we combine these instruments to shorten timelines while staying fully compliant. You don't have to navigate German administration, that's our job.
entreprises.rolesLead: A clear split, so you know exactly what we take care of.
entreprises.rolesUs6: Following up with the candidate after arrival
entreprises.rolesYou1: A precise description of roles and skills
entreprises.rolesYou3: Launching the accelerated procedure, if desired
entreprises.rolesYou4: A welcome and support during onboarding
entreprises.garantiesLead: Clear commitments, because international recruitment requires trust.
entreprises.gar1Body: A dedicated contact, from the first conversation through to integration.
entreprises.gar2Title: Recruitment seen through to the end
entreprises.gar2Body: We support every case through to onboarding.
entreprises.gar3Body: Strict adherence to the Skilled Immigration Act and its procedures.
entreprises.gar4Body: Fair recruitment principles, including the WHO code for healthcare.
entreprises.gar5Body: We stay present for integration that lasts.
entreprises.gar6Title: A commitment to find a solution
entreprises.gar6Body: If a profile isn't the right fit, we look for an alternative together with you.
entreprises.partenaireLead: We're building a network on both sides of the bridge. A partner can be local (training school, language center, organization in Central Africa) or based in Germany (company, healthcare institution, organization).
entreprises.contactTitle: Tell us about your recruitment need
entreprises.contactLead: Describe the roles you need to fill: we'll get back to you with matching profiles and a clear timeline. No-obligation conversation.

entreprisesFaq.q1: Is the recruitment compliant with German law?
entreprisesFaq.a1: Yes. We work within the Skilled Immigration Act: qualification recognition, skilled worker visa, and compliant procedures.
entreprisesFaq.q2: How long does the process take?
entreprisesFaq.a2: It depends on the profile and its level of preparation (language, qualification recognition). After analyzing your need, we give you a realistic timeline.
entreprisesFaq.q3: What German level do the candidates have?
entreprisesFaq.a3: We train them up to the level required by the role, often B2 for care occupations and public-facing roles.
entreprisesFaq.a4: The accelerated skilled worker procedure is one you, the employer, can launch with the central foreigners authority. It processes qualification recognition and the visa as a priority, reducing timelines.
entreprisesFaq.a5: It's the recognition partnership, in place since 2024. It allows the candidate to come first, then finalize their qualification recognition on-site, for a faster start.
entreprisesFaq.a6: Yes. We apply fair recruitment principles, including the WHO code for health workers, and favor lasting placements.
entreprisesFaq.q7: In which sectors do you recruit?
entreprisesFaq.a7: Healthcare, construction and trades, hospitality, technical industry, IT, and logistics.
entreprisesFaq.q8: Do I need an existing job offer to get started?
entreprisesFaq.a8: No. You describe your need to us, and we present matching profiles. We adapt the process to your situation.

entreprisesServices.title: Our recruitment services
entreprisesServices.subtitle: A placement service built for German companies facing a labor shortage.
entreprisesServices.section1Body: We recruit and train Cameroonian and Central African candidates in the occupations where your needs are strongest: healthcare, hospitality, construction, industry, IT.
entreprisesServices.section2Body: Every profile you review has taken a German placement test. You never receive applications below the required level.
entreprisesServices.section3Body: We advise you on the legal framework for recruiting qualified foreign workers (Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz) and the visa process on the candidate's side.

entreprisesProfils.title: Profiles & sectors available
entreprisesProfils.subtitle: A pool of trained, verified candidates, organized by shortage sector.
entreprisesProfils.section1Body: Healthcare, hospitality, construction & trades, industry & technical trades, IT: the sectors where German demand is strongest and where we focus our training.
entreprisesProfils.section2Body: Every candidate visible in our pool has been reviewed by our team: identity, German level, qualification or experience in the target occupation.
entreprisesProfils.section3Body: Access to full profiles (CV, contact details) is reserved for company accounts validated by our team, to protect our candidates' privacy.

entreprisesPartenariat.title: Become a partner company
entreprisesPartenariat.subtitle: Karriere Fähre works with German companies in sectors facing labor shortages, and is continually growing this network.
entreprisesPartenariat.section1Title: A partnership, not a one-off placement
entreprisesPartenariat.section1Body: Becoming a partner means building a lasting relationship with us: anticipating your recurring staffing needs rather than handling them one at a time.
entreprisesPartenariat.section2Title: What we expect from a partner
entreprisesPartenariat.section2Body: A clear legal framework, a serious welcome for the candidate on arrival, and transparent communication about the roles offered.
entreprisesPartenariat.section3Body: Priority access to our candidate pool, dedicated support, and visibility on our partners page.

entreprisesProcessus.title: Our process
entreprisesProcessus.subtitle: Visa, Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz (Skilled Immigration Act): the legal framework explained simply.
entreprisesProcessus.section1Body: Since the Skilled Immigration Act (Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz), Germany has made it easier for non-European skilled workers to enter shortage occupations. We track this closely to keep every case secure.
entreprisesProcessus.section2Title: The visa process on the candidate side
entreprisesProcessus.section2Body: Employment contract, qualification recognition if needed, consular appointment: we support the candidate at every step, in coordination with you.
entreprisesProcessus.section3Body: You provide the contract and the role details. We coordinate the case preparation and follow-up through to the candidate's arrival.

entreprisesPourquoi.title: Why Central Africa
entreprisesPourquoi.subtitle: What Cameroonian and Central African candidates bring to your company.
entreprisesPourquoi.section1Body: Cameroon and Central Africa have a young population looking for meaningful training and serious international career opportunities.
entreprisesPourquoi.section2Body: French-speaking backgrounds and, for some candidates, prior exposure to German, make it easier to learn quickly up to B2 level.
entreprisesPourquoi.section3Title: An agency that knows both sides
entreprisesPourquoi.section3Body: Founded by a German-French-Cameroonian entrepreneur, Karriere Fähre selects and trains its candidates with a precise understanding of your expectations as a German employer.

metiers.title: The occupations hiring in Germany
metiers.subtitle: In short: Germany lacks skilled workers across many sectors. Healthcare, construction, hospitality, industry, IT, and logistics offer real opportunities: we guide you to the path and trade suited to your profile, and train you in German.
metiers.contexteLead: An aging population and a dynamic economy create a lasting shortage of skilled labor. To fill it, Germany has opened widely to foreign talent, under a dedicated legal framework (Skilled Immigration Act).
metiers.contexteBody: For you, that means real demand across several sectors, and a clear path to get there, provided you're well prepared. That's our job.
metiers.secteursTitle: Every occupation hiring, at a glance
metiers.secteursLead: Each sector, its roles (with German job titles), and the language level generally expected.
metiers.eligibiliteLead: Whatever the sector, four things shape your plan, and we help with each one:
metiers.crit1Body: B2 level required. We train you up to B2, even starting from scratch.
metiers.crit2Body: A qualification, a diploma, or solid experience in the trade.
metiers.crit3Body: We prepare the Anerkennung of your qualification, the trickiest step.
metiers.crit4Body: Employers look for profiles that settle for the long term.
metiers.parcoursTitle: From application to job, in 4 steps
metiers.step1Body: We identify the sector and path suited to your profile.
metiers.step2Body: German up to the required level, plus trade vocabulary.
metiers.step3Body: Recognition, application file, and skilled worker visa.
metiers.step4Body: Starting your role in Germany, with our follow-up.
metiers.finalTitle: Find the occupation that fits you
metiers.finalText: Get your profile assessed: we'll tell you which sector and path suit you, and what steps lie ahead.

metiersFaq.q1: Which occupations are hiring most in Germany?
metiersFaq.a1: Healthcare, construction and trades, hospitality, technical industry, IT, and logistics are among the sectors under the most pressure.
metiersFaq.a2: B2 level is required for all our paths. We support you up to B2, even starting from scratch.
metiersFaq.a3: Depending on the path: a recognized qualification, a professional certification, or solid experience can open doors. We assess your profile to find the right path.
metiersFaq.a4: Many occupations require recognition (Anerkennung). We build the file with you to avoid mistakes that cost months.
metiersFaq.q5: How do I know which sector fits me?
metiersFaq.a5: Get your profile assessed: based on your qualification, experience, and German level, we guide you to the sector or sectors best suited to you.

metiersOffre.reassureTitle: With Karriere Fähre, you are not on your own
